1.1: The second book of the naḇi Ezra son of Serayah, son of Azaryah, son of Ḥilqiyahu, son of Shallum, son of Tsaḏoq, son of Aḥituḇ,
1.2: son of Aḥiyah, son of Pineḥas, son of Ĕli, son of Amaryah, son of Azaryah, son of Merĕmoth, son of Arna, son of Uzzi, son of Buqqi, son of Aḇishua, Pineḥas, son of Eli’ezer,
1.3: son of Aharon, of the tribe of Lĕwi; who was captive in the land of the Maḏites, in the reign of Artaḥshashta meleḵ of Paras.
1.4: And the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to me, saying,
1.5: “Go your way, and show My people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against Me; that they may tell their children’s children.
1.6: “Because the sins of their fathers are increased in them; for they have forgotten Me, and have offered to foreign mighty ones.
1.7: “Am not I even He who brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage? But they have provoked Me to wrath, and despised My counsels.
1.8: “Pull off the hair from your head, and throw all evil upon them, for they have not been obedient to My Law, but are a rebellious people.
1.9: “How long shall I endure them, to whom I have done so much good?
1.10: “I have destroyed many melaḵim for their sakes; I have struck down Pharaoh with his servants and all his strength.
1.11: “I have destroyed all the nations before them, and in the east I have scattered the people of two provinces, even of Tsor and Tsiḏon, and have slain all their enemies.
1.12: “Therefore you speak to them, saying, ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
1.13: “I led you through the sea and from the beginning gave you a wide and safe passage. I gave you Mosheh for a leader, and Aharon for a kohĕn.
1.14: “I gave you light in a pillar of fire, and I have done great wonders among you; yet have you forgotten Me,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.15: ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty, “The quails were as a sign to you; I gave you booths for your safety; still you grumbled there,
1.16: and did not overcome in My Name for the destruction of your enemies, but even to this day you still grumble.
1.17: “Where is the good that I have done for you? When you were hungry and thirsty in the wilderness, did you not cry out to Me,
1.18: saying, ‘Why have You brought us into this wilderness to kill us? It would have been better for us to have served the Mitsrites, than to die in this wilderness!’
1.19: “Then I took pity on your groaning, and gave you manna to eat; so you ate bread of messengers.
1.20: “When you were thirsty, did I not split the rock, and waters flowed out to your fill? For the heat I covered you with the leaves of the trees.
1.21: “I divided among you a fruitful land, I drove out the Kena’anites, the Perizzites and the Pelishtites before you. What more shall I do for you?” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.22: ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty, “When you were in the wilderness, at the river of the Amorites, thirsting, and blaspheming My Name,
1.23: I did not send fire for your blasphemies, but threw a branch in the water, and made the river sweet.
1.24: “What shall I do unto you, O Ya’aqoḇ? You, Yahuḏah, would not obey me. I shall turn myself to other nations, and to them I shall give My Name, that they may guard My Laws.
1.25: “Seeing you have forsaken Me, I shall also forsake you. When you desire for Me to show favor to you, I shall show no kindness to you.
1.26: “Whenever you call upon Me, I do not hear you; for you have defiled your hands with blood, and your feet are swift to commit murder.
1.27: “It is not as though you have forsaken Me, but your own selves,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.28: ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty, “Have I not treated you as a father his sons, as a mother her daughters, and a nurse her young infants,
1.29: that you would be my people, and I should be your Elohim; that you would be my children, and I should be your Father?
1.30: “I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings; but now, what shall I do to you? I shall throw you out from My presence.
1.31: “When you offer unto Me, I shall turn my face from you; for I have rejected your Moedim, your new moons, and your circumcisions.
1.32: “I sent to you My servants the neḇi’im, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I shall require of your hands,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
1.33: ‘Thus says the Almighty, “Your house is laid waste, I shall cast you out as the wind does stubble.
1.34: “And your children shall not be fruitful; for they have despised My Command, and done that which is evil before Me.
1.35: “I shall give your houses to a people that shall come; who having not yet heard of Me, shall believe Me; to whom I have showed no signs, yet they shall do what I have Commanded them.
1.36: “They have seen no neḇi’im, yet they call their sins to remembrance, and acknowledge them.
1.37: “I call to witness the favor of the people to come, whose little ones rejoice in gladness, and though they have not seen Me with bodily eyes, yet in spirit they believe the Word that I say.
1.38: “And now brother, see what esteem; and see the people that come from the East,
1.39: to whom I shall give for leaders, Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq and Ya’aqoḇ, Hoshĕa, Amos and Miḵah, Yo’ĕl, Oḇaḏyah and Yonah,
1.40: Naḥum and Ḥaḇaqquq, Tsephanyah, Ḥaggai, Zeḵaryah and Mal’aḵi, who is also called a messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.” ’

10.1: “And it so came to be, that when my son had entered into his wedding room, he fell down, and died.
10.2: “Then we all put out the lamps, and all my neighbors rose up to comfort me; so I remained quiet to the evening of the second day.
10.3: “And it came to be, when they had all finished comforting me, so that I might be quiet; then I rose up by night and fled, and came here to this field, as you see.
10.4: “And now I plan not to return to the city, but to stay here, and to neither eat nor drink, but to continually mourn and fast until I die.”
10.5: Then I left the thoughts in which I was, and spoke to her in wrath, saying,
10.6: “You foolish woman above any other, do you not see our mourning, and what comes upon us?
10.7: “For Tsiyon, our mother, is full of all grief, and humbled greatly, mourning bitterly.
10.8: “And now, seeing we all mourn and are sad, for we are all in grief, and you are grieved for one son?
10.9: “For ask the earth, and it shall tell you, that it is the one which ought to mourn for the fall of so many that grow upon it.
10.10: “For out of it came all in the beginning, and out of it shall all others come, and see, almost all of them walk to destruction, and a multitude of them shall be completely uprooted.
10.11: “Who then should make more mourning than it, which has lost so great a multitude; and not you, who are grieved for but one?
10.12: “But if you say to me, ‘My lamentation is not like that of the earth, because I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I brought forth with pains, and bore with sorrows,
10.13: but the earth not so; for the multitude present in it have gone as they came, according to the way of the earth.’
10.14: “Then I say to you, as you have brought forth with labor; even so the earth has also given its fruit, namely man, ever since the beginning to He who made it.
10.15: “Now therefore keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear that which has befallen you with good courage.
10.16: “For if you acknowledge the judgment of Elohim to be righteous, you shall both receive your son in time, and shall be praised among women.
10.17: “Go your way then into the city to your husband.”
10.18: And she said to me, “That I shall not do. I shall not go into the city, but I shall die here.”
10.19: So I proceeded to speak further to her, and said,
10.20: “Do not do so, but let me give counsel; for how many are the adversities of Tsiyon? Be comforted in regard to the sorrow of Yerushalayim.
10.21: “For you see that our Miqdash is laid waste, our altar broken down, our Hĕyḵal destroyed;
10.22: our harp is laid low, our song is put to silence, our rejoicing is at an end, the light of our lampstand is put out, the ark of our Covenant is plundered, our qodesh objects are defiled, and our name that we are called by is almost profaned; our children are put to shame, our kohenim are burned, our Lĕwites have gone into captivity, our maidens are defiled, and our wives ravished; our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men are brought into bondage, and our strong men have become weak;
10.23: and greatest of all, the seal of Tsiyon has now lost its esteem; for it is delivered into the hands of those who hate us!
10.24: “And therefore shake off your great sadness, and put away the great number of sorrows, that the Almighty may be kind to you again, and the Most High shall give you rest and ease from your labor.”
10.25: And it came to be while I was talking with her, see, her face suddenly shone exceedingly, and her face lit up, so that I was afraid of her, and wondered what it might be.
10.26: And see, suddenly she made a very great fearful cry, so that the earth shook at the noise of the woman.
10.27: And I looked, and see, the woman appeared to me no more, but there was a city built, and a large place revealed itself from the foundations; then I was afraid, and cried with a loud voice, and said,
10.28: “Where is Uri’ĕl the messenger, who came to me in the beginning? For he has caused me to fall into many trances, for my end is turned into corruption, and my prayer to rebuke.”
10.29: And as I was speaking these words, see, he came to me, and looked upon me.
10.30: And see, I lay as one dead, and my understanding was removed; and he took me by the right hand, and comforted me, and stood me on my feet, and said to me,
10.31: “What is the matter with you? And why are you so worried? And why is your understanding and the thoughts of your heart troubled?
10.32: And I said, “Because you have forsaken me, and yet I did according to your words, and I went into the field, and look, I have seen, and still see that which I am unable to express!”
10.33: And he said to me, “Stand up like a man, and I shall advise you.”
10.34: Then I said, “Speak on, my master; only do not forsake me, lest I die lacking my expectancy.
10.35: “For I have seen what I did not know, and heard what I do not know.
10.36: “Or are my senses deceived, or is my being in a dream?
10.37: “Now therefore I plead that you reveal to your servant about this vision.”
10.38: Then he answered me, and said, “Listen to me, and I shall inform you, and tell you why you are afraid; for the Most High shall reveal many secrets to you.
10.39: “He has seen that your way is righteous; in that you grieve continually for your people, and make great lamentation for Tsiyon.
10.40: “This therefore is the meaning of the vision which you recently saw:
10.41: “You saw a woman mourning, and you began to comfort her;
10.42: but now you see the likeness of the woman no more, but a built city appeared to you.
10.43: “And whereas she told you of the death of her son, this is the interpretation:
10.44: “This woman, whom you saw is Tsiyon; and when she spoke to you, even she whom you see as a built city,
10.45: for when she said to you that she has been barren thirty years; those are the thirty years in which there was no offering made in her.
10.46: “But after thirty years Shelomoh built the city and offered offerings, and then bore the barren a son.
10.47: “And when she told you that she nourished him with labor; that was the dwelling in Yerushalayim.
10.48: “But when she said to you, ‘My son coming into his marriage room had a fall, and died.’ This was the destruction that came upon Yerushalayim.
10.49: “And, see, you saw her likeness, and because she mourned for her son, you began to comfort her; and these matters which have taken place are to be opened unto you.
10.50: “For now the Most High sees that you are sincerely grieved, and suffer in your whole heart for her, so He has showed you the brightness of her esteem, and the comeliness of her loveliness.
10.51: “And therefore I asked that you remain in the field where no house was built;
10.52: for I knew that the Most High would show this to you.
10.53: “Therefore I commanded you to go into the field, where no foundation of any building was,
10.54: for no building of man is able to stand in the place where the Most High begins to show His city.
10.55: “And therefore do not fear, nor let your heart be afraid, but go your way in, and see the loveliness and greatness of the building, as much as your eyes be able to see;
10.56: and then you shall hear as much as your ears may comprehend.
10.57: “For you are baruḵ above many others, and are called by the Most High; for so few are.
10.58: “But tomorrow at night you shall remain here;
10.59: and the Most High shall show you visions of what is above, which the Most High shall do for those who dwell on the earth in the last days.” So I slept that night and the next, as he commanded me.

11.1: Then I saw a dream, and see, an eagle came up from the sea, which had twelve feathered wings and three heads.
11.2: And I looked, and see, it spread its wings over all the earth, and all the winds of the air blew on it, and were gathered together.
11.3: And I looked, and out of its wings grew other opposing wings; and they became little wings but smaller.
11.4: And its heads were at rest - the head in the midst was greater than the others, yet it rested with the others.
11.5: And I looked, and see, the eagle flew with its wings, and reigned on earth, and over those who dwelt in it.
11.6: And I saw that all under the shamayim were subject to it, and no man spoke against it, no, not one creature on earth.
11.7: And I looked, and see, the eagle rose up on its talons, and spoke to its wings, saying,
11.8: “Do not watch all at once; every one sleep in its own place, and watch in turn;
11.9: but let the heads be reserved for the last.”
11.10: And I looked, and see, the voice did not come out of its heads, but from the midst of its body.
11.11: And I numbered its opposing wings, and, see, there were eight of them.
11.12: And I looked, and see, on the right side there arose one wing, and reigned over all the earth;
11.13: and so it was, that when it reigned, its end came, and its place appeared no more; so the next following stood up and reigned, and reigned a long time.
11.14: And it came to be, that when it reigned, its end also came, as the first, so that it appeared no more.
11.15: Then a voice came unto it, and said,
11.16: “Listen, you who have ruled over the earth so long; I say this to you, before the time you are no longer seen:
11.17: “None after you shall attain to your time, neither to the half of it.”
11.18: Then the third arose, and reigned as the other before, and also appeared no more.
11.19: So it came to be with all the remaining, one after another, so that each one reigned, and then appeared no more.
11.20: Then I looked, and see, in the course of time the wings that followed stood up on the right side, that they might also reign; and some of them reigned, but in a little while they appeared no more;
11.21: for some of them rose up, but did not reign.
11.22: After this I looked, and see, the twelve wings appeared no more, nor the two little wings;
11.23: and there was no more on the eagle’s body, but three heads that rested, and six little wings.
11.24: Then I also saw that two little wings separated themselves from the six, and remained under the head that was on the right side; for the four remained in their place.
11.25: And I looked, and see, the wings that were under the wing thought to appoint themselves and to reign.
11.26: And I looked, and see, there was one appointed, but soon it appeared no more.
11.27: And the second went away sooner than the first.
11.28: And I looked, and see, the two that remained also thought within themselves to reign;
11.29: and when they thought so, see, one of the heads that was at rest awoke - that which was in the midst; for it was greater than the two other heads.
11.30: And then I saw that the other two heads were joined with it,
11.31: and see, the head was turned with those who were with it, and ate up the two wings under the wing that would have reigned.
11.32: But this head put the whole earth in fear, and reigned over all those who dwelt on the earth with great oppression; and it governed over the world more than all the wings that had been.
11.33: And after this I looked, and see, the head that was in the midst suddenly appeared no more, as the wings.
11.34: But the two heads remained, which in like manner also ruled over the earth, and over those who dwelt in it.
11.35: And I looked, and see, the head on the right side devoured that which was on the left side.
11.36: Then I heard a voice, which said to me, “Look in front of you, and consider that which you see.”
11.37: And I looked, and saw what was like a roaring lion chased out of the forest; and I saw that it sent out the voice of a man to the eagle, and said,
11.38: “Listen, I shall speak with you, and the Most High says to you:
11.39: ‘Are you not that which remains of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in My world, that the end of their times might come through them?
11.40: ‘And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fear, and over the whole circle of the earth with much evil oppression; and it dwelt upon the earth for a long time with deceit.
11.41: ‘For you have judged the earth, but not with truth.
11.42: ‘For you have afflicted the meek, you have hurt the peaceable, you have loved the false, and destroyed the dwellings of those who brought forth fruit, and have thrown down the walls of those who did you no harm.
11.43: ‘Therefore your wrongdoing has come up before the Most High, and your pride to the Almighty.
11.44: ‘The Most High has also looked upon the proud times, and see, they have ended, and its abominations are complete.
11.45: ‘And therefore you eagle, appear no more, nor your horrible wings, nor your evil wings nor your wicked heads, nor your evil claws, nor your whole worthless body;
11.46: ‘That all the earth may be refreshed, and may return, being delivered from your violence, and that it may have expectancy for the judgment and kindness from He who made it.’ ”

12.1: And it came to be, while the lion spoke these words to the eagle, I looked,
12.2: and see, the head that remained and the four wings appeared no more, and the two went forward and appointed themselves to reign, and their reign was short, but full of unrest.
12.3: And I looked, and see, they appeared no more, and the whole body of the eagle was burned so that the earth was in great fear; then I woke from great fear out of the troubled trance of my mind, and said to my spirit,
12.4: “See, you have done this to me, because you search out the ways of the Most High.
12.5: “Yet see, I am weary in my mind, and very weak in my spirit; and there is little strength in me, for the great fear with which I was afflicted this night.
12.6: “Therefore I now plead to the Most High, that He shall comfort me to the end.”
12.7: And I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, if I have found favor before Your eyes, and if I am made right with You before many others, and if my prayer indeed comes up before Your face;
12.8: encourage me then, and show me, Your servant, the interpretation and clear meaning of this fearful vision, that You may fully comfort my being.
12.9: “For You have judged me worthy to show me the last days.”
12.10: And He said to me, “This is the interpretation of the vision:
12.11: “The eagle, which you saw come up from the sea, is the reign which was seen in the vision of your brother Dani’ĕl.
12.12: “But it was not explained to him, therefore I now declare it to you.
12.13: “See, the days shall come, that a reign shall rise up on earth, and it shall be feared above all the reigns that were before it.
12.14: “And twelve melaḵim shall reign in it, one after another;
12.15: of which the second shall begin to reign, and shall have more time than any of the twelve.
12.16: “This is what the twelve wings signify, which you saw.
12.17: “As for the voice which you heard speak, and that you saw to not go out from the heads, but from the midst of its body, this is the interpretation:
12.18: “At the time of that reign great struggles shall arise, and it shall stand in danger of failing; nevertheless it shall not fall then, but shall be restored again to its beginning.
12.19: “And as you saw the eight small wings underneath clinging to its wings, this is the interpretation:
12.20: “Eight melaḵim shall arise within it, whose times shall be short, and their years swift.
12.21: “And two of them shall perish, the middle of its time approaching; four shall be kept until their end begins to approach; but two shall be kept until the end.
12.22: “And as you saw three heads resting, this is the interpretation:
12.23: “In the last days the Most High shall raise up three reigns, and in this shall renew many matters, and they shall have the reign of the earth,
12.24: and of those who dwell in it, with much oppression, above all those who were before them; therefore they are called the heads of the eagle.
12.25: “For these are they who shall accomplish its wickedness, and who shall complete its latter end.
12.26: “And when you saw that the great head appeared no more, it signifies that one of them shall die on his bed, but with pain.
12.27: “As for the two that remain, they shall be slain with the sword.
12.28: “For the sword of the one shall devour the other; but in the end it shall fall through the sword itself.
12.29: “And as you saw two wings under the wings passing over the head that is on the right side;
12.30: this signifies that these are they, whom the Most High has kept to the end; this is the short reign full of trouble, as you saw.
12.31: “And the lion, whom you saw rising up out of the forest roaring, and speaking to the eagle, and rebuking it for its unrighteousness with all the words which you have heard;
12.32: “This is ha’Mashiaḥ, whom the Most High has kept for them and for their wickedness unto the end; He shall reprove them, and shall reproach them for their cruelty.
12.33: “For He shall stand them before Him alive in judgment, and shall rebuke them, and reprove them.
12.34: “For He shall deliver the rest of My people with kindness - those who have been scattered from My borders, and He shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.
12.35: “This is the dream that you saw, and these are the interpretations.
12.36: “Only you have been approved to know this secret of the Most High,
12.37: therefore write all these that you have seen in a book, and hide them;
12.38: and teach them to the wise of the people, whose hearts you know may understand and guard these secrets.
12.39: “But wait here yourself yet seven days more, that it may be shown you whatever pleases the Most High to declare to you.” And with that he went his way.
12.40: And it came to be, when all the people saw that the seven days had passed, and I had not come again into the city, they all gathered together, from the least to the greatest, and came to me, and said,
12.41: “In what have we offended you, and what evil have we done against you, that you leave us, and sit here in this place?
12.42: “Of all the neḇi’im, only you are left, as a cluster of the vineyard and as a candle in a dark place, and as a haven or ship preserved from the storm.
12.43: “Are not the evils which have come upon us enough?
12.44: “If you forsake us, how much better it would have been for us, if we had also been burned in the midst of Tsiyon!
12.45: “For we are no better than those who died there; and they wept with a loud voice.” Then I answered them, and said,
12.46: “Take courage, O Yisra’ĕl; and do not be grieved, you house of Ya’aqoḇ;
12.47: for the Most High has remembered you, and the Almighty has not forgotten you in your trial.
12.48: “As for me, I have not forsaken you, neither have I departed from you; but have come to this place to pray for the desolation of Tsiyon, and that I might seek kindness for the humiliation of your Miqdash.
12.49: “And now, everyone make your way home, and after these days I shall come to you.”
12.50: So the people made their way into the city, as I commanded them;
12.51: But I remained in the field seven days, as the messenger commanded me; and ate only the flowers of the field in those days, and my food was from the plants.

13.1: And it came to be after seven days, I dreamed a dream by night;
13.2: and see, a wind rose from the sea, that stirred up all its waves.
13.3: And I looked, and see, the wind formed the likeness of a Man from the heart of the sea, and the Man flew with the clouds of the shamayim; and when He turned his face to look, all that was seen under Him trembled.
13.4: And whenever the voice went out of His mouth, all those who heard His voice burned, as the earth falls away when it feels the fire.
13.5: And after this I looked, and see, a crowd of men without number was gathered together, from the four winds of the shamayim, to overcome the Man who came out of the sea.
13.6: But I looked, and see, He had carved Himself a great mountain, and rose up on it.
13.7: And I tried to see the region or place from which the mountain was carved, and I could not.
13.8: And after this I looked, and see, all those who were gathered together to overcome Him were very afraid, and yet were bold to fight.
13.9: And look, as He saw the violence of the crowd that came, He neither lifted up His hand, nor held a sword, nor any weapon of battle;
13.10: but I only saw that He sent what looked like a blast of fire out of His mouth, and a flaming breath out of His lips, and He threw out a storm of sparks out of His tongue.
13.11: And they were all mingled together; the blast of fire, the flaming breath, and the great storm; which fell with violence on the crowd that was prepared to fight, and burned up every one of them, so that suddenly none was seen of the innumerable crowd, but only dust and a smell of smoke. When I saw this I was afraid.
13.12: Afterward I saw the same Man come down from the mountain, and called to Himself another peaceful crowd.
13.13: And many people came to Him, of whom some were glad, some were sorrowful, and some of them were bound, and some brought others with offerings; then I was sick through great fear, and I woke, and said,
13.14: “You have shown Your servant these wonders from the beginning, and have counted me worthy that You should receive my prayer;
13.15: now show me the interpretation of this dream also.
13.16: “For as I consider in my understanding, woe to those who are left in those days and much more woe to those who are not left behind!
13.17: “For those who are not left shall be grieved.
13.18: “Now I understand that which is laid up in the latter days, which shall come upon them, and to those who are left behind.
13.19: “Therefore they have come into great danger and much distress, as these dreams declare.
13.20: “Yet it is better for he who is in danger to come to these, than to pass out of the world as a cloud, and not see that which shall come to be in the last days.” And He answered me, and said,
13.21: “I shall show you the interpretation of the vision, and I shall open to you that which you have asked.
13.22: “When you spoke of those who are left behind, this is the interpretation:
13.23: “He who shall endure the danger in that time guards himself; those who have fallen into danger are those who have works, and belief toward the Almighty.
13.24: “Know this therefore, that those who are left behind are happier than those who are dead.
13.25: “This is the meaning of the vision: When you saw a Man coming up from the midst of the sea;
13.26: “He is the One whom Elohim the Most High has kept for a long time, whom by Himself shall deliver His creation; and He shall lead those who are left behind.
13.27: “And when you saw, that a blast of wind and fire and storm came out of His mouth;
13.28: and that He held neither sword, nor any weapon of battle, but that His rushing in destroyed the whole crowd that came to overcome Him; this is the interpretation:
13.29: “See, the days are coming, when the Most High shall begin to deliver those who are on the earth.
13.30: “And those who dwell on the earth shall be astonished at His coming.
13.31: “And one shall begin to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one reign against another.
13.32: “And the time shall be when these come to pass, and the signs take place which I showed you before, and then My Bĕn shall be declared, whom you saw as a Man ascending.
13.33: “And when all the people hear His voice, every man in their own land shall leave the battle they have against one another,
13.34: and an innumerable crowd shall gather together, as you saw them, coming with desire to overcome Him in battle.
13.35: “But He shall stand on the top of Mount Tsiyon,
13.36: and Tsiyon shall come, and shall be shown to all men, being prepared and built, as you saw the mountain carved without hands.
13.37: “And He, My Bĕn shall rebuke the wicked deeds of those nations, who have fallen into the storm for their wicked life;
13.38: “And shall lay their evil thoughts before them, and the torture with which they shall begin to be tortured, which are like flames; and He shall destroy those without works by the Law which is comparable to Me.
13.39: “And when you saw that He gathered another peaceful multitude to Himself;
13.40: those are the ten tribes, which were carried away captive out of their own land in the time of Hoshĕa the meleḵ, whom Shalmaneser the meleḵ of Ashshur led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so they came to another land.
13.41: “But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the gentiles, and go out to a distant land, where mankind had not dwelt,
13.42: that there they might guard their Laws, which they had not kept in their own land.
13.43: “And they entered into Perath by the narrow places of the River,
13.44: for at that time the Most High showed signs for them, and held the flood, till they had passed over.
13.45: “For there was a great way to go through that land, of a year and a half; and that region is called Ḥarosheth.
13.46: “Then they dwelt there until the last days; and when they begin to come,
13.47: the Most High shall hold the springs of the River again, that they may go through; therefore you saw the multitude at peace.
13.48: “But those who are left behind of your people are those who are found within My borders.
13.49: “Now when He destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, He shall defend His people that remain.
13.50: “And then He shall show them great wonders.”
13.51: Then I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, show me this: Why have I seen the Man coming up from the midst of the sea?”
13.52: And He said to me, “As you could neither seek out nor know that which is in the depths of the sea; even so no man on earth shall see My Bĕn, or those who are with Him, but in His time of day.
13.53: “This is the interpretation of the dream which you saw, and why you alone are enlightened,
13.54: for you have forsaken your own way, and applied your diligence to My Law, and sought it.
13.55: “You have ordered your life in wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.
13.56: “And therefore I have showed you the treasures of the Most High; after another three days I shall speak further to you, and declare to you mighty and wondrous matters.”
13.57: Then I went out into the field, giving great praise and thanks to the Most High because of His wonders which He does in due time;
13.58: And because he governs the times, and these fall in their seasons. And I sat there three days.

14.1: And it came to be on the third day, I sat under a terebinth, and see, a voice came out of a bush opposite me, and said, “Ezra, Ezra.”
14.2: And I said, “Here I am, Aḏonai.” And I stood up on my feet.
14.3: Then He said to me, “I clearly revealed Myself to Mosheh in the bush, and talked with him, when My people were slaves in Mitsrayim;
14.4: and I sent him and led My people out of Mitsrayim, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him with Me many days,
14.5: and told him great wonders, and showed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying,
14.6: ‘These words you shall declare, and these you shall hide.’
14.8: “Lay up in your heart the signs that I have shown, and the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations which you have heard;
14.9: for you shall be taken away from all, and from now on you shall remain with My Bĕn, and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.
14.10: “For the world has lost its youth, and the times begin to grow old.
14.11: “For the world is divided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it have gone already, and half of a tenth part;
14.12: and there remains that which is after the half of the tenth part.
14.13: “Now therefore put your house in order, and reprove your people; comfort those who are in distress, and now renounce that which is corrupt.
14.14: “Let go of your mortal thoughts, throw away the burdens of man, put off now the weak nature,
14.15: and lay aside the thoughts that are most grievous to you, and hasten to flee from these times.
14.16: “For even greater evils than those which you have seen shall come to be after this.
14.17: “For see how much the world weakens through age; therefore evil increases much more upon those who dwell in it.
14.18: “For truth has fled far away, and falsehood is close at hand; for the vision which you seen now hastens to come.”
14.20: “See, Aḏonai, I shall go as You have commanded me, and reprove the people who are present; but those who are born after, who shall admonish them? Thus the world lays in darkness, and those who dwell in it are without light.
14.21: “For Your Law has been burned, therefore no one knows that which is done by You, or the work that shall begin.
14.22: “But if I have found favor before You, send the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh into me, and I shall write all that has been done in the world since the beginning, which was written in Your Law, that men may find Your Way, and that those who live in the latter days may live.”
14.23: And He answered me, saying, “Go your way, gather the people together, and say to them, not to seek you for forty days.
14.24: “But see, prepare for yourself many writing tablets, and take with you Serayah, Daḇriyah, Shelemyah, Ĕythan, and Asi’ĕl, these five who are able to write swiftly;
14.25: and come here, and I shall light a lamp of understanding in your heart, which shall not be put out, till that which you shall begin to write is complete.
14.26: “And when you are done, you shall publish some, and some you shall show secretly to the wise; tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write.”
14.27: Then I went out as He commanded, and gathered all the people together, and said,
14.29: “At the beginning our fathers were sojourners in Mitsrayim, from where they were delivered;
14.30: and received the Law of Ḥai, which they did not guard, which you have also transgressed after them.
14.31: “Then the land, even the land of Tsiyon, was divided among you by lot; but your fathers, and you have done unrighteousness, and have not guarded the Ways which the Most High Commanded you.
14.32: “And because He is a righteous Judge, in due time, He took from you that which He had given you,
14.33: and now you are here, and your brothers are among you.
14.34: “Therefore if you humble your own understanding, and transform your hearts, you shall be kept alive and after death you shall obtain kindness.
14.35: “For after death the judgment shall come, when we shall live again; and then the names of the righteous shall be revealed, and the works of the wicked shall be declared.
14.36: “Therefore let no man come to me now, nor seek me for forty days.”
14.37: So I took the five men, as He commanded me, and we went to the field, and remained there.
14.38: And the next day, see, a voice called to me saying, “Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink.”
14.39: Then I opened my mouth, and see, he brought me a cup, which was full of water, but the color of it was like fire.
14.40: And I took it, and drank; and when I had drunk from it, my heart spoke with understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for the remembrance in my spirit was strengthened;
14.41: and my mouth was opened, and no longer closed.
14.42: And the Most High gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote the extraordinary night visions that were related, which they did not know; and they sat forty days, and wrote in the day, and ate their bread at night.
14.43: As for me; I spoke during the day, and did not keep silent by night.
14.44: In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.
14.45: And it came to be, when the forty days were complete, that the Most High spoke, saying, “The first that you have written publish openly, that the worthy and unworthy may read it;
14.46: but guard the seventy last, that you may deliver them only to those who are wise among the people;
14.47: for in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the river of knowledge.”

15.1: “See, speak in the ears of My people the words of neḇuah, which I shall put in your mouth,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.2: “And cause them to be written on paper; for they are trustworthy and true.
15.3: “Do not fear the schemes against you, do not let the unbelief of those who speak against you trouble you.
15.4: “For all the unbelieving shall die in their unbelief.
15.5: “Look,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I shall bring plagues upon the world; the sword, scarcity of food, death and destruction.
15.6: “For wickedness has polluted the whole earth exceedingly, and their evil works are complete.
15.8: “I shall hold My tongue no more in regard to their wickedness, which they do evilly, neither shall I tolerate them in that which they wickedly engage themselves; see, the blood of the innocent and righteous cries out to Me, and the beings of the righteous protest continually.
15.9: “And therefore,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I shall surely avenge them, and receive all the innocent blood from among them to Me.
15.10: “See, My people are led as a flock to the slaughter. I shall not allow them to now dwell in the land of Mitsrayim;
15.11: but I shall bring them with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and smite Mitsrayim with plagues, as before, and shall destroy all its land.
15.12: “Mitsrayim shall mourn, and its foundation shall be smitten with the plague and punishment that Elohim brings upon it.
15.13: “Those who till the ground shall mourn, for their seed shall fail through the blight and hail, and from a frightening storm.
15.14: “Woe to the world and those who dwell in it!
15.15: “For the sword and their destruction draws near, and one people shall stand up and fight against another, with swords in their hands.
15.16: “For there shall be uproar among men, and they shall invade one another with no regard for their melaḵim nor princes, and the course of their actions shall stand in their strength.
15.17: “A man shall desire to go into a city, and not be able;
15.18: for because of their pride the cities shall be troubled, the houses shall be destroyed, and men shall be afraid.
15.19: “Man shall have no compassion for his neighbor, but shall destroy their houses with the sword, and plunder their goods, because of the lack of bread, and of great distress.
15.20: “See,” says Elohim, “I shall call together all the melaḵim of the earth to revere Me, who are from the rising of the sun - from the south, from the east and Leḇanon - to turn themselves one against another, and repay what they have done to them.
15.21: “As they still do today to My chosen, so I shall also do, and repay into their bosom.” Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim;
15.22: “My right hand shall not spare the sinners, and My sword shall not cease over those who shed innocent blood on the earth.”
15.23: The fire of His wrath has gone forth and consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners, like straw that is kindled.
15.24: “Woe to those who sin, and do not guard My Commands!” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.25: “I shall not spare them. Go your way, you unbelieving children, do not defile My Miqdash!”
15.26: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 knows all those who sin against Him, therefore He gives them over to death and destruction.
15.27: For now the plagues have come upon the whole earth and you shall remain in them; for Elohim shall not deliver you, because you have sinned against Him.
15.28: Look, a horrible vision, and its appearance from the east:
15.29: Where the nations of the dragons of Araḇia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon the earth, that all those who hear them fear and tremble.
15.30: Also the Parasians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the forest, and they shall come in great strength, and engage in battle with them, and shall destroy a portion of the land of Ashshur.
15.31: And then the dragons, remembering their nature, shall have the upper hand; and if they ally together, turning themselves in great strength to pursue them,
15.32: then these shall be troubled, and silenced by their strength, and shall flee.
15.33: And the enemy shall besiege them from the land of Ashshur, and consume some of them, and within their army shall be fear and dread, and strife among their melaḵim.
15.34: Look! Clouds from the east and from the north to the south, and they are very horrible to look upon, full of wrath and storm.
15.35: They shall clash against one another, and they shall bring down a great number of storms on the earth, even their own storm; and from the sword there shall be blood to the waist,
15.36: and dung of man to the camel’s hock.
15.37: And there shall be great fear and trembling on the earth; and those who see the wrath shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.
15.38: And then great storms shall come from the south and from the north and another part from the west,
15.39: and strong winds shall rise from the east, and shall prevail; and the cloud which He raised up in wrath, and the storm stirred up causing fear toward the east and west wind, shall be destroyed.
15.40: The great and mighty clouds shall billow full of wrath, and the storm, with which they make all the earth afraid, and those who dwell in it; and they shall pour out a horrible storm over every high and lofty place:
15.41: fire, and hail, and flying swords, and many waters, so that all fields and all rivers, shall overflow with the exceedingly great amount of waters.
15.42: And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the forest and grass of the field, and its grain.
15.43: And they shall move steadily onto Baḇel, and cause her fear.
15.44: They shall come to her, and besiege her, pouring out the storm and all wrath upon her; then the dust and smoke shall go up to the shamayim, and all those who are around her shall bewail her.
15.45: And those who remain under her shall do service to those who have put her in fear.
15.46: And you, Asia, who shares in the expectancy of Baḇel, and are the esteem of her person -
15.47: woe to you, you wretch, because you have made yourself like her, and have adorned your daughters with whoring, that they might please and boast in your lovers, who have always desired to commit whoring with you.
15.48: You have followed she who is hated in all her works and devices; “Therefore,” says Elohim,
15.49: “I shall send plagues upon you: widowhood, poverty, scarcity of food, sword and pestilence, to waste your dwellings with destruction and death.
15.50: “And the esteem of your strength shall be dried up as a flower, the burning that is sent upon you shall rise.
15.51: “You shall be weakened as a poor woman with stripes, and like one flogged with wounds, so you shall not be received by your mighty lovers!
15.52: “Would I have proceeded against you so fervently,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.53: “If you had not always slain My chosen, exulting and clapping your hands, and speaking over their dead, when you were drunk?
15.55: “The reward of your whoring shall be in your bosom, therefore you shall be repaid.
15.56: “As you have done to My chosen,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “even so shall Elohim do to you, and shall hand you over to evil.
15.57: “Your children shall die of hunger, and you shall fall by the sword. Your cities shall be broken down, and all those in the field shall perish by the sword.
15.58: “Those who are in the mountains shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drink their own blood, from hunger of bread, and thirst of water.
15.59: “Grieving, you shall pass through the sea, and receive plagues again,
15.60: and as they pass they shall rush on the treacherous city, and shall destroy some portion of your land, and consume part of your esteem, and shall return to Baḇel, which was destroyed.
15.61: “And you shall be thrown down by them as stubble, and they shall be as fire to you;
15.62: and shall consume you and your cities, your land and your mountains and all your woods; and they shall burn up your fruitful trees with fire.
15.63: “They shall carry your children away captive, and see, what you have, they shall plunder it, and destroy the loveliness of your face.”

16.1: Woe to you, Baḇel, and Asia! Woe to you, Mitsrayim and Aram!
16.2: Gird up yourselves with sackcloth and hair; bewail your children, and mourn, for your destruction is at hand.
16.3: A sword is sent upon you, and who shall turn it back?
16.4: A fire is sent among you, and who shall quench it?
16.5: Plagues are sent upon you, and who is he who would drive them away?
16.6: Shall any man drive away a hungry lion in the forest? Or shall anyone quench the fire in stubble, when it has begun to burn?
16.7: Would one turn again the arrow that is shot from a strong archer?
16.8: The Almighty Aḏon sends the plagues, and who is he who drives them away?
16.9: A fire shall go forth from His wrath, and who is he who would quench it?
16.10: He shall throw lightnings, and who would not fear? He shall thunder, and who would not be afraid?
16.11: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 threatens, and who would not be utterly beaten to dust at His presence?
16.12: The earth and its foundations quake, the sea rises up with waves from the deep, and its waves are troubled, and also the fish in it, before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and before the esteem of His power;
16.13: for His right hand is strong that bends the bow, His arrows that He shoots are sharp, and do not miss, when they begin to be shot into the ends of the world.
16.14: See, the plagues are sent, and shall not return again, until they come upon the earth.
16.15: The fire is kindled, and shall not be put out, till it consumes the foundation of the earth.
16.16: As an arrow which is shot by a mighty archer does not return, even so the plagues that are sent upon the earth shall not return again.
16.17: Woe is me! Woe is me! Who shall deliver me in those days?
16.18: The beginning of sorrows and great mourning; the beginning of scarcity of food and great death; the beginning of fighting, and the powers shall stand in fear; the beginning of evils! What shall I do when these evils come?
16.19: See, scarcity of food and plague, distress and anguish are sent as scourges for correction;
16.20: but for all these they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor ever remember the scourges.
16.21: See, food shall cost so little on earth, that they shall think themselves to be well at ease, and then evil shall grow on earth: the sword, scarcity of food and great confusion.
16.22: For many of those who dwell on earth shall perish from scarcity of food; and the others who escape the hunger, the sword shall destroy.
16.23: And the dead shall be thrown out as dung, and there shall be no one to comfort them; for the earth shall be a waste, and the cities shall be thrown down.
16.24: There shall be no one left to till the earth, and to sow it;
16.25: the trees shall give fruit, but who shall gather them?
16.26: The grapes shall ripen, and who shall tread them? For all places shall be barren of mankind,
16.27: so that one shall desire to see another, and to hear his voice.
16.28: For there shall be ten left of a city, and two of the field, who shall hide themselves in the thick forests, and in the caves of the rocks;
16.29: as in an orchard of olives there are three or four olives left on every tree;
16.30: or as there are left some clusters when a vineyard is gathered, by those who diligently seek through the vineyard.
16.31: Even so there shall be three or four left by those who search their houses with the sword in those days.
16.32: And the earth shall be laid waste, and its fields shall grow old, and its roads and all its paths shall grow full of thorns, because no one travels through there.
16.33: The maidens shall mourn, having no bridegrooms; the women shall mourn, having no husbands; their daughters shall mourn, having no helpers.
16.34: Their bridegrooms shall be destroyed in the fighting, and their husbands shall perish for scarcity of food.
16.35: Hear now these and understand them, you servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.36: This is the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, receive it; do not believe the mighty ones of whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke.
16.37: See, the plagues draw near, and do not delay.
16.38: As when a woman with child in the ninth month brings forth her son, within two or three hours of her birth, great pains encompass her womb - such pains, when the child is coming forth that do not ease for a moment -
16.39: even so the plagues to come upon the earth shall not be eased, and the world shall mourn, and sorrows shall come upon it from every side.
16.40: Hear my words, O my people; prepare for battle, and in those evils be as sojourners on the earth.
16.41: He who sells, let him be as he who flees; and he who buys, as one who loses;
16.42: he who deals in merchandise, as he who has no profit from it; and he who builds, as he who shall not dwell in it;
16.43: he who sows, as if he shall not reap; so also he who plants the vineyard, as he who shall not gather the grapes;
16.44: those who marry, as those who shall bear no children; and those who do not marry, as the widowers.
16.45: And therefore those who labor, labor in vain;
16.46: for foreigners shall reap their fruits and plunder their goods, overthrow their houses and take their children captive, for they shall bring forth children into captivity and scarcity of food.
16.47: “And those who obtain their merchandise by robbery, the more they adorn their cities, their houses, their possessions and their own person;
16.48: the more shall I be wroth with them for their sin.” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.49: As a whore envies an upright honest and virtuous woman;
16.50: so righteousness hates wickedness, when she adorns herself, and accuses her to her face, when He comes who shall defend the one who diligently searches out every sin on the earth.
16.51: And therefore do not be like her, nor her works.
16.52: For yet a little, and wickedness shall be taken away from the earth, and righteousness shall reign among you.
16.53: Let not the sinner say that he has not sinned; for Elohim shall burn coals of fire upon his head, who says before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim and his esteem, “I have not sinned!”
16.54: See, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 knows all the works of man, their schemes, their thoughts, and their hearts;
16.55: who spoke but the word, “Let the earth be made.” and it was made; “Let the shamayim be made,” and it was created.
16.56: By His word the stars were made, and He knows the number of them.
16.57: He searches the deep, and its treasures; He has measured the sea, and what it contains.
16.58: He has shut the sea in the midst of the waters, and with His word He has suspended the earth upon the waters.
16.59: He spreads out the shamayim like a span; He has founded it upon the waters.
16.60: He has made springs of water in the desert, and pools upon the tops of the mountains, that the floods might pour down from the high rocks to water the earth.
16.61: He made man, and put his heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding,
16.62: and indeed the Ruaḥ of Ĕl Shaddai; who made all and searches out all that is hidden in the secret places of the earth.
16.63: Surely He knows your plans, and the thoughts of your hearts, even those who sin, and want to hide their sin.
16.64: Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 searches out all your works exactly, and he shall put you all to shame.
16.65: And when your sins are produced, you shall be ashamed before all, and your own sins shall be your accusers in that Day.
16.66: What shall you do, or how shall you hide your sins before Elohim and His messengers?
16.67: See, Elohim Himself is the Judge; revere Him! Cease from your sins, and forget your wickednesses, to no longer I strive in them forever; so Elohim shall lead you out, and deliver you from all trouble.
16.68: For see, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you, and they shall take some of you away, and feed the idle, with that which is offered to idols.
16.69: And those who consent to them shall be mocked and reproached, and trampled under foot.
16.70: For in every place and in the neighboring cities, there shall be a great uprising against those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.71: They shall be like madmen, sparing none, but continue ravaging and destroying those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.72: For they shall lay waste and take away their goods, and throw them out of their houses.
16.73: Then those who are My chosen shall be known; and they shall be tried as gold in the fire.
16.74: “Hear, O you My beloved,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “See, the days of trouble are at hand, but I shall deliver you from them.
16.75: “Do not be afraid, neither doubt; for Elohim is your guide,
16.76: and the guide of those who guard My Commands and Orders,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, “do not let your sins weigh you down, and do not let your wickednesses rise up.
16.77: “Woe to those who are bound up in their sins and covered with their wickedness like a field overgrown with bushes, and its path covered with thorns, so that no man may travel through!
16.78: “It is left naked, and is thrown into the fire to be consumed by it.”

2.1: ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them My Commands by My servants the neḇi’im; whom they would not hear, but despised My counsels.
2.2: “The mother that bore them says to them, ‘Go your way, you children; for I am a widow and forsaken.
2.3: ‘I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness I have lost you; for you have sinned before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and done that which is evil before Him.
2.4: ‘But what shall I now do for you? I am a widow and forsaken; go your way, O My children, and ask kindness from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.’
2.5: “As for Me, O father, I call upon you for a witness over the mother of these children, who would not guard My Covenant;
2.6: that you bring them to confusion, and their mother to ruin, that there may be no offspring from them.
2.7: “Let them be scattered abroad among the gentiles, let their names be blotted out from the earth; for they have despised My Covenant.
2.8: “Woe to you, Ashshur, you that hide the unrighteous within you! O you wicked people, remember what I did to Seḏom and Amorah;
2.9: whose land lies in lumps of tar and piles of ashes; even so I shall do the same to those who do not listen to Me.” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty.’ ”
2.10: Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to Ezra, “Tell my people that I shall give them the reign of Yerushalayim, which I would have given to Yisra’ĕl.
2.11: “I shall also take their esteem to Myself, and give others the everlasting dwellings, which I had prepared for them.
2.12: “They shall have the tree of ḥai for an ointment of sweet savor; they shall neither labor, nor be weary.
2.13: “Go, and you shall receive; pray that your days are few, that they may be shortened. The reign is already prepared for you; watch!
2.14: “Call the shamayim and earth to witness; for I have broken the evil in pieces, and created the good; for I live.” Says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.15: “Mother, embrace your children, and bring them up with gladness, make their feet as steady as a pillar; for I have chosen you.” Says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.16: “And those who are dead I shall raise up again from their places, and bring them out of the graves; for I have acknowledged My Name in Yisra’ĕl.
2.17: “Do not fear, you mother of the children; for I have chosen you,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.18: “For your help I shall send My servants Yeshayahu and Yirmeyahu, after whose counsel I have qadosh and prepared for you twelve trees laden with different fruits,
2.19: and as many fountains flowing with milk and honey, and seven mighty mountains, on which there grow roses and lilies, whereby I shall fill your children with joy.
2.20: “Do right to the widow, judge for the fatherless, give to the poor, defend the orphan, clothe the naked,
2.21: heal the broken and the weak, do not mock a lame man, defend the crippled, and let the blind man come into the sight of My brightness.
2.22: “Guard the old and young within your walls.
2.23: “Wherever you find the dead, take them and bury them, and I shall give you the first place in My resurrection.
2.24: “Remain, O My people, and take your rest, for your rest is still to come.
2.25: “Nourish your children, O you good nurse; establish their feet.
2.26: “As for the servants whom I have given you, not one of them shall perish; for I shall require them from among your number.
2.27: “Do not be weary; for when the day of trouble and heaviness comes, others shall weep and be sorrowful, but you shall be joyful and have abundance.
2.28: “The gentiles shall envy you, but they shall be able to do naught against you.” Says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.29: “My hands shall cover you, so that your children shall not see She’ol.
2.30: “Be joyful, O you mother, with your children; for I shall deliver you,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.31: “Remember your children who sleep, for I shall bring them out from the breadth of the earth, and show kindness to them; for I am kind,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Almighty.
2.32: “Embrace your children until I come and show kindness to them; for My wells run over, and My favor does not fail.”
2.33: I Ezra received a command from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on mount Ḥorĕḇ, that I should go to Yisra’ĕl; but when I came to them, they disregarded and despised the Command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.34: And therefore I say unto you, “O you gentiles that hear and understand, look for your Shepherd, He shall give you everlasting rest; for He is near at hand, who shall come at the end of the world.
2.35: “Be ready for the reward of the reign, for the everlasting light shall shine upon you forever.
2.36: “Flee the shadow of this world, receive the joy of your esteem; I witness of my Savior openly.
2.37: “O receive the gift that is given you, and be glad, giving thanks to He who has led you to the reign of the shamayim.
2.38: “Arise and stand, see the number of those who are sealed at the Feast of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
2.39: who have departed from the shadow of this world, and have received garments of esteem from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.40: “Take your number, O Tsiyon, and enclose those in you who are clothed in white, who have filled the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.41: “The number of your children, whom you long for is filled; plead the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that your people, who have been called from the beginning, may be qadosh.”
2.42: I Ezra saw upon Mount Tsiyon a great people whom I could not number, and they all praised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with songs.
2.43: And in the midst of them there was a young Man of tall stature - taller than all the rest; and upon every one of their heads He placed crowns, and was more exalted; at which I marveled at greatly.
2.44: So I asked the messenger, and said, “Master, who are these?”
2.45: He answered and said to me, “These are those who have put off the mortal garments, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the Name of Elohim; now they are crowned, and receive palms.”
2.46: Then I said to the messenger, “What young Man is this who crowns them, and gives them palms in their hands?”
2.47: So he answered and said to me, “It is the Son of Elohim, whom they have confessed in the world.” Then I began to greatly commend those who stood so steadfastly for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.48: Then the messenger said to me, “Go your way, and tell my people how great and how many are the wonders of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, which you have seen.”

3.1: In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city, I was in Baḇel, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts overwhelmed my heart;
3.2: for I saw the desolation of Tsiyon, and the wealth of those who dwelt in Baḇel.
3.3: And my spirit was greatly moved, so that I began to speak words full of reverence to the Most High, and said,
3.4: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, You spoke in the beginning, when You established the earth, and by You alone, and commanded the dust,
3.5: and gave a body to Aḏam without being, which was the workmanship of Your hands, and breathed into him the breath of life, and he was made living before You.
3.6: “And You led him into paradise, which Your right hand had planted, before the earth ever appeared.
3.7: “And You gave a Command to him to love Your Way; which he transgressed, and immediately You appointed death in him and in his generations, from whom came nations, tribes, people, and clans, without number.
3.8: “And all people walked after their own desire, and acted arrogantly before You, and despised Your Commands.
3.9: “And again it came to be, You brought the flood upon those who dwelt on the earth, and destroyed them.
3.10: “And it came to be in each of them, that as death was to Aḏam, so was the flood to these.
3.11: “Nevertheless You left one of them, namely, Noaḥ with his household, from whom came all righteous men.
3.12: “And it came to be, that when those who dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, and had brought forth many children, and were a great people, they began again to be more wicked than the first.
3.13: “Now when they lived so wickedly before You, You chose a man from among them, whose name was Aḇraham.
3.14: “You loved him, and You showed Your desire to him alone,
3.15: and made an everlasting Covenant with him, promising to him that You would never forsake his seed.
3.16: “And to him you gave Yitsḥaq, and to Yitsḥaq you also gave Ya’aqoḇ and Ĕsaw. As for Ya’aqoḇ You chose him for Yourself, and put Ĕsaw aside; and so Ya’aqoḇ became a great multitude.
3.17: “And it came to be, that when You led his seed out of Mitsrayim, You brought them up to Mount Sinai.
3.18: “And bowing the shamayim, You established the earth, moved the whole world, and made the depths to tremble, and troubled the men at that time.
3.19: “And Your esteem passed through four gates, of fire and of earthquake and of wind and of cold; that You might give the Law to the seed of Ya’aqoḇ, and Commandments to the generation of Yisra’ĕl.
3.20: “And yet You did not take away from them a wicked heart, that Your Law might bring forth fruit in them.
3.21: “For the first Aḏam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so are all those who are descended from him.
3.22: “Thus sickness was made permanent; and the Law in the heart of the people with the evil root; so that the good departed, and the evil still stayed.
3.23: “So the days passed, and the years were brought to an end; then You raised You up a servant, named Dawiḏ,
3.24: whom You commanded to build a city for Your Name, and to offer incense and offerings to You within it.
3.25: “When this was done many years, then those who inhabited the city forsook You,
3.26: and acted in all manner even as Aḏam and all his generations had done; for they also had a wicked heart.
3.27: “And so You gave Your city over into the hands of Your enemies.
3.28: “Are their deeds then any better who inhabit Baḇel, that they should therefore have the reign over Tsiyon?
3.29: “For when I came there, and had seen unrighteousness’s without number, and my being saw many evil-doers in these thirty years, so that my heart failed me.
3.30: “For I have seen how You endure those sinning and have spared evil-doers; and have destroyed Your people, and have preserved Your enemies, and have not declared it.
3.31: “I do not remember how to depart from this way. Are those of Baḇel then better than those of Tsiyon?
3.32: “Or is there any other people that knows You besides Yisra’ĕl, or what generation has believed Your Covenants so much as Ya’aqoḇ?
3.33: “And yet their reward does not appear, and their labor has no fruit; for I have gone here and there among the gentiles, and I see that they overflow in wealth, and do not think upon Your Commands.
3.34: “Now therefore weigh our wickedness in the balance, and also theirs who dwell on the earth; and so shall Your Name be found nowhere but in Yisra’ĕl.
3.35: “Or when was it that those who dwell on the earth have not sinned in Your sight, or what people have so kept Your Commands?
3.36: “You shall find that Yisra’ĕl by name has kept Your Orders; but not the gentiles.”

4.1: And the messenger that was sent to me, whose name was Uri’ĕl, answered me
4.2: and said, “Your heart has gone too far regarding this world, and do you think to understand the way of the Most High?”
4.3: Then I said, “Yes, my master.” And he answered me, and said, “I have been sent to show you three ways, and to put forth three situations before you;
4.4: of which if you declare to me one, I shall also show you the way that you desire to see, and I shall show you from where the wicked heart comes.”
4.5: And I said, “Speak on, my master.” Then he said to me, “Go your way, weigh the weight of fire, or measure the blast of the wind, or recall the day that is past.”
4.6: Then I answered and said, “What man is able to do this, that you should ask such matters of me?”
4.7: And he said to me, “If I should ask you how many dwellings are in the midst of the sea, or how many springs are in the source of the deep, or how many fountains are above the expanse, or which are the exits of She’ol, or the entrances of paradise?
4.8: “However you might say to me, ‘I never went down into the deep, neither as yet into She’ol, nor did I ever climb up into the shamayim.’
4.9: “Nevertheless I have only asked you of the fire and wind, and of the day through which you have passed, and of that from which you cannot be separated, and yet, you give me no answer of them.”
4.10: He said further to me, “That which is your own, and what you have grown up with, you cannot know.
4.11: “How then should your mind be able to know the way of the Most High, and the world being now outwardly corrupted, to understand the corruption that is clearly in my sight?”
4.12: Then I said to him, “It would be better that we were not at all, than that we should still live in wickedness, and to suffer, and not to know why.”
4.13: He answered me, and said, “I went into a forest into a plain, and the trees took counsel
4.14: and said, ‘Come, let us go and fight against the sea that it may depart before us, and that we may make more forests.’
4.15: “The floods of the sea also similarly took counsel, and said, ‘Come, let us go up and subdue the forests of the plain, that there also we may make ourselves more territory.”
4.16: The plan of the forest was in vain, for the fire came and consumed it.
4.17: The plan of the floods of the sea came likewise to naught, for the sand stood up and stopped them.
4.18: If you were judge now between these two, whom would you begin to declare right, or whom would you condemn?
4.19: I answered and said, “Truly it is a foolish thought that they have both devised, for the ground is given to the forest, and the sea also has its place to hold its floods.”
4.20: Then he answered me, and said, “You have given a right judgment, but why do you not judge yourself also?
4.21: “For as the ground is given to the forest, and the sea to its floods; even so those who dwell on the earth may understand naught but that which is on the earth; and He who dwells above the shamayim may only understand that which is above the height of the shamayim.”
4.22: Then I answered and said, “Please, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, let me have understanding.
4.23: “For it was not my thought to be curious of the ways above, but of such that pass by us daily, namely, why Yisra’ĕl is given up as a reproach to the gentiles, and for what cause the people whom You have loved are given over to wicked nations, and why the Law of our forefathers is brought to naught, and the written Covenants nullified?
4.24: “And we pass away out of the world as grasshoppers, and our life is astonishment and fear, and we are not worthy to obtain kindness.
4.25: “What shall He then do for His Name by which we are called? Of these matters I have asked.”
4.26: Then he answered me, and said, “The more you search, the more you shall marvel; for the world hastens to pass away,
4.27: and cannot understand that which is promised to the righteous in time to come; for this world is full of unrighteousness and sickness.
4.28: “But concerning that of which you ask me, I shall tell you; for the evil is sown, but its destruction has not yet come.
4.29: “If therefore that which is sown is not removed, and if the place where the evil is sown is not turned over, then it cannot become sown with good.
4.30: “For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Aḏam from the beginning, and how much wickedness has it produced to this time? And how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing comes?
4.31: “Consider now for yourself, what great fruits of wickedness the grain of evil seed has brought forth.
4.32: “And when the heads are cut down, which are without number, how great a floor they shall fill!”
4.33: Then I answered and said, “How, and when shall these come to pass? Why are our years few and evil?”
4.34: And he answered me, saying, “Do not hasten more than the Most High; for it is worthless for your haste to be more than His, for you have over-exceeded.
4.35: “Did not the beings of the righteous also ask question of these in their rooms, saying, ‘How long shall I have expectancy in this way? When does the reward of our harvest come?’
4.36: “And to these Uri’ĕl the chief messenger answered them, and said, ‘When the number of seeds has been filled in you; for He has weighed the world in the balance.
4.37: ‘By measure He has measured the times; and by number He has numbered the times; and He does not move nor stir them, until the said measure is filled.’ ”
4.38: Then I answered and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, we are all full of unrighteousness,
4.39: and possibly it is for our sake that the floors of the righteous are not filled, because of the sins of those who dwell on the earth!”
4.40: So he answered me, and said, “Go your way to a woman with child, and ask her when she has completed her nine months, if her womb may keep the birth any longer within her.”
4.41: Then I said, “No master, she cannot.” And he said to me, “The rooms of beings in the grave are like the womb of a woman;
4.42: for as a woman in childbirth hastens to escape the necessity of the childbirth; even so do these places hasten to deliver those who are entrusted to them.
4.43: “From the beginning, look, what you desire to see, it shall be shown you.”
4.44: Then I answered and said, “If I have found favor in Your sight, and if it is possible, and if I am able,
4.45: show me then whether there is more to come than is past, or more past than is to come.
4.46: “What is past I know, but what is to come I do not know.”
4.47: And he said to me, “Stand on the right, and I shall explain the parable to you.”
4.48: So I stood and looked, and see, a hot burning torch passed before me; and it came to be that when the flame had passed I looked, and see, the smoke still remained.
4.49: After this there passed before me a watery cloud, and sent down much rain with a storm; and when the stormy rain had passed, the drops still remained.
4.50: Then he said to me, “Consider for yourself; as the rain is more than the drops, and as the fire is greater than the smoke; so the quantity which is past is greater, but the drops and the smoke remained.”
4.51: Then I prayed, and said, “Do you think I shall live until that time? Or what shall come to be in those days?”
4.52: He answered me, and said, “As for the signs of which you ask me, I may tell you of them in part; but regarding your life, I am not sent to show you; for I do not know it.

5.1: “But regarding the signs, see, the days shall come, that those who dwell upon the earth shall be taken in a great number, and the Way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of belief.
5.2: “But wickedness shall be increased above that which you now see, or that you have heard long ago.
5.3: “And the land, which you now see to have a root, you shall see suddenly laid waste.
5.4: “But if the Most High grants you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and a third of the moon in that day.
5.5: “And blood shall drip from wood, and the stone shall give its cry, and the people shall be troubled;
5.6: and one shall rule, whom those who dwell upon the earth do not expect, and the birds shall take flight away together.
5.7: “And the Sea of Seḏom shall throw out fish, and make a noise in the night, which many have not known; but they shall all hear the sound of it.
5.8: “There shall also be confusion in many places, and the fire shall be often sent out again, and the wild beasts shall change their places, and women during uncleanness shall bring forth monsters.
5.9: “And salt water shall be found with the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then knowledge shall hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into its secret room,
5.10: and shall be sought by many, and yet not be found. Then unrighteousness and lack of self control shall be multiplied on earth.
5.11: “One land shall also ask another, and say, ‘Has righteousness that makes a man righteous passed through you?’ And it shall say, ‘No.’
5.12: “At the same time men shall have expectancy, but do not obtain; they shall labor, but their ways shall not prosper.
5.13: “To show you such signs I have permission; and if you pray again, and weep as now, and fast seven days, you shall hear yet greater matters.”
5.14: Then I woke, and an extreme fear went through my entire body, and my mind was so troubled, that I fainted.
5.15: So the messenger that had come to talk with me held me, comforted me, and stood me up on my feet.
5.16: And on the second night it came to be, that She’alti’ĕl the leader of the people came to me, saying, “Where have you been, and why is your countenance so heavy?
5.17: “Do you not know that Yisra’ĕl is entrusted to you in the land of their captivity?
5.18: “Rise therefore, and eat bread, and do not forsake us, as the shepherd that leaves his flock in the hands of cruel wolves.”
5.19: Then I said to him, “Go away from me, and do not come near me.” And he heard what I said, and went from me.
5.20: And so I fasted seven days, mourning and weeping, as Uri’ĕl the messenger commanded me.
5.21: And after seven days it came to be, that the thoughts of my heart were very grievous to me again,
5.22: and my being recovered the spirit of understanding, and I began to speak with the Most High again,
5.23: and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, over every forest of the earth, and all the trees in it, You have chosen Your one and only vine.
5.24: “And of all lands of the whole earth You have chosen Your one cistern, and of all the flowers of it; one lily.
5.25: “And of all the depths of the sea You have filled Your one river. And of all cities built, You have qadosh Tsiyon unto Yourself.
5.26: “And of all the birds that are created You have named Your one dove. And of all the beasts that are made You have supplied Your one sheep.
5.27: “And among all the multitudes of people You have chosen Your one people. And unto this people, whom You loved, You gave a Law that is acceptable for all.
5.28: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, why have You given this one people over to many, and upon the one root You have prepared others, and why have You scattered Your one and only people among many?
5.29: “And those who denied Your promises, and did not believe Your Covenants, have trodden them down.
5.30: “If You hated Your people so much, should You punish them with Your own hands?”
5.31: Now when I had spoken these words, the messenger that came to me the night before was sent to me,
5.32: and said to me, “Hear me, and I shall instruct you; listen to the word that I speak, and I shall tell you more.”
5.33: And I said, “Speak on, master.” Then he said to me, “You are greatly troubled in heart for the sake of Yisra’ĕl. Do you love that people more than He who made them?”
5.34: And I said, “No, master, but of very grief I have spoken, for my kidneys pain me every hour, while I labor to understand the Way of the Most High, and to seek out part of His Right-Ruling.”
5.35: And he said to me, “You cannot.” And I said, “Why, master? For what was I born then, or why was my mother’s womb not my grave, that I might not have seen the trouble of Ya’aqoḇ, and the wearisome toil of the race of Yisra’ĕl?”
5.36: And he said to me, “Number for me that which has not yet come; gather together for me the dross that is scattered abroad, make the flowers that are withered green again,
5.37: open for me the places that are closed, and bring forth for me the winds that in them are shut up, show me the image of a voice; and then I shall declare to you that which you labor to know.”
5.38: And I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, who may know these, but He whose dwelling is not with men?
5.39: “As for me, I am unwise; how may I then speak of these matters of which You ask me?”
5.40: Then He said to me, “As you are unable to do any of these that I have spoken of, even so you cannot find out My judgment, or the love in the end that I have promised to My people.”
5.41: And I said, “See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You are still near to those who are reserved till the end; but what shall they do who have been before me, or we who are here now, or those who shall come after us?”
5.42: And He said to me, “I shall liken My judgment to a circle; as there is no slackness for the last, even so there is no swiftness for the first.”
5.43: So I answered and said, “Could you not make those who have been made, and are now, and who are to come, at once; that You might show Your judgment sooner?”
5.44: Then He answered me, and said, “The creature cannot hasten more than the Maker; neither could the world hold at once those who shall be created within.”
5.45: And I said, “As You have said to Your servant, that You, who gives life to all, have given life at once to the creatures that You have created, and the creation bore it; even so it might also bear those who are now present at once.”
5.46: And He said to me, “Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her, ‘If you bring forth children, why not do them all together, but one after another?’ Ask her therefore to bring forth ten children at once.”
5.47: And I said, “She cannot; but must do it over a span of time.”
5.48: Then He said to me, “Even so have I given the womb of the earth to those who are sown in it in their times.
5.49: “For as a young child cannot bring forth those that belong to the aged, even so have I subjected the world which I created.”
5.50: And I asked, and said, “Seeing You have now given me an occasion, I shall proceed to speak before You; for our mother, of whom You have told me that she is young, now draws near to age.”
5.51: He answered me, and said, “Ask a woman that bears children, and she shall tell you.
