5.52: “Say to her, ‘Why are those whom you have now brought forth like those who were before, but smaller in size?’
5.53: “And she shall answer you, ‘Those who are born in the strength of youth are of one form, and those who are born in the time of age, when the womb fails, are otherwise.’
5.54: “Consider yourself also therefore, how you are less of stature than those who were before you,
5.55: and so are those who come after you lesser than you, as the creation which now begins to age, and has passed over the strength of youth.”
5.56: Then I said, “Please 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, if I have found favor in Your sight, show Your servant by whom You visit your creation.”

6.1: And He said to me, “In the beginning, when the earth was made, before the borders of the world stood, or the winds ever blew;
6.2: before it thundered and lightning struck, or before the foundations of paradise were laid;
6.3: before the lovely flowers were seen, or ever the moveable powers were established, before the innumerable multitude of messengers were gathered together,
6.4: or before the heights of the shamayim were lifted up, before the measures of the expanse were named, or before the footstool of Tsiyon was established,
6.5: and before the present years were sought out, and before the deeds of those who now sin were turned, before those who have gathered belief for a treasure were sealed.
6.6: “Then I considered these, and they all were made through Me alone, and through none other; by Me they shall also be ended, and by none other.”
6.7: Then I answered and said, “What shall be the dividing of the times, or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of that which follows?”
6.8: And he said to me, “From Aḇraham to Yitsḥaq, when Ya’aqoḇ and Ĕsaw were born to him, Ya’aqoḇ’s hand first held the heel of Ĕsaw.
6.9: “For Ĕsaw is the end of the world, and Ya’aqoḇ is the beginning of that which follows.
6.10: “The hand of man is between the heel and the hand; other questions, Ezra, do not ask.”
6.11: Then I answered and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, if I have found favor in Your sight,
6.12: please, show Your servant the end of Your signs, of which You showed me in part the last night.”
6.13: So He answered and said to me, “Stand up on your feet, and hear a mighty sounding voice.
6.14: “And there shall be a great shaking; but the place where you stand shall not be moved.
6.15: “And so, when it sounds do not be afraid; for the word is of the end, and the foundation of the earth understands.
6.16: “And why? Because the sound of these trembles and is moved; for it knows that the end of these must be changed.”
6.17: And it came to be, that when I heard it I stood up on my feet, and listened, and see, there was a voice that spoke, and the sound of it was like the sound of many waters.
6.18: And it said, “See, the days come, that I shall begin to draw near, and to visit those who dwell on the earth,
6.19: and shall begin to make inquiry of them, what harm they have done unrighteously with their wickedness, and when the affliction of Tsiyon shall be complete;
6.20: and when the world, that shall begin to vanish away, is finished, then I shall show these signs: the Books shall be opened before the expanse, and they all shall see together.
6.21: “And children a year old shall speak with their voices, the women with child shall bring forth children prematurely of three or four months old, and they shall live, and be raised up.
6.22: “And suddenly the sown places shall appear unsown, the full storehouses shall suddenly be found empty;
6.23: and the trumpet shall give a sound, which when every man hears, they shall be suddenly afraid.
6.24: “At that time friends shall fight against one another as enemies, and the earth shall stand in fear with those who dwell in it; the springs of the fountains shall stand still, and in three hours they shall not flow.
6.25: “Whoever remains from all these that I have told you shall escape, and see My deliverance, and the end of your world.
6.26: “And those who are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth; and the heart of inhabitants shall be changed, turned into another spirit.
6.27: “For evil shall be blotted out, deception shall be quenched.
6.28: “As for belief, it shall flourish; corruption shall be overcome, and the truth, which has been so long without fruit, shall be declared.”
6.29: And when he talked with me, see, I looked little by little upon him before whom I stood.
6.30: And these words he said to me, “I have come to show you the time of the night to come.
6.31: “If you pray further, and fast seven days again, I shall tell you greater matters by day than you have heard.
6.32: “For your voice is heard before the Most High; for the Almighty has seen your righteous dealing, He has also seen your blamelessness, which you have had since your youth.
6.33: “And therefore He has sent me to show you all these, and to say to you, ‘Take courage and do not fear.’
6.34: “And do not hasten to think worthlessly about the past times, so that you do not hasten from the latter times.”
6.35: And it came to be after this, that I wept again, and fasted seven days in similar manner, that I might complete the three weeks which he told me.
6.36: And on the eighth night my heart was tortured within me again, and I began to speak before the Most High;
6.37: for my spirit burned greatly, and my being was in distress.
6.38: And I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You spoke from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and said, ‘Let the shamayim and earth be made,’ and Your word became a perfect work.
6.39: “And then the Ruaḥ and darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man’s voice was not yet formed.
6.40: “Then You commanded a good light to come forth from Your treasures, that Your work might appear.
6.41: “On the second day You created the breath of the expanse, and commanded it to divide, and to make a division between the waters, that one part would go up, and the other remain beneath.
6.42: “On the third day You commanded the waters to be gathered into a seventh part of the earth; six parts You dried up, and kept them, in order that some of these being planted by Elohim and tilled might serve You.
6.43: “For as soon as Your word went forth the work was made,
6.44: for immediately there was great and innumerable fruit, and many and varied pleasures for the taste, and flowers of unchangeable color, and fragrances of wondrous smell; and these were created the third day.
6.45: “On the fourth day You commanded that the sun should shine, and the moon give its light, and the stars should be in order;
6.46: and commanded them to do service to man, who was to be made.
6.47: “On the fifth day You spoke to the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, that it should bring forth living creatures, birds and fish; and so it came to be.
6.48: “For the silent, lifeless water brought forth living creatures at the command of Elohim, that all people might praise Your wondrous works.
6.49: “Then You appointed two living creatures, the one you called Behĕmoth, and the other Liwiathan,
6.50: and separated the one from the other; for the seventh part, namely, where the water was gathered together, would not hold them both.
6.51: “Unto Behĕmoth You gave one part, which was dried up the third day, that it should dwell in the same part, in which are a thousand hills:
6.52: “But to Liwiathan You gave the seventh part, that is, the waters; and have kept it to be consumed by whom You want, and when.
6.53: “On the sixth day You gave command to the earth, that it should bring forth beasts, cattle, and creeping creatures before You.
6.54: “And after these, Aḏam also, whom You made master of all your creatures; from him we have all come, and also the people whom You have chosen.
6.55: “All this have I spoken before You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because You made the world for our sakes.
6.56: “As for the other people, who also come from Aḏam, You have said that they are naught, but are as spittle; and have likened the abundance of them to a drop that falls from a vessel.
6.57: “And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, see, these gentiles, who have always been regarded as naught, have begun to be masters over us, and to consume us.
6.58: “But we Your people, whom You have called Your first-born, Your only brought forth, and Your dearly beloved, are given into their hands.
6.59: “If the world is now made for our sakes, why do we not possess an inheritance with the world? How long shall this endure?”

7.1: And when I had finished speaking these words, the messenger who had been sent to me the nights before was sent to me.
7.2: And he said to me, “Rise, Ezra, and hear the words that I have come to tell you.”
7.3: And I said, “Speak on, my master.” Then he said to me, “The sea is put in a wide place, that it might be deep and great.
7.4: “But if it were that the entrance were narrow, and like a river;
7.5: who then could go into the sea to look upon it, and to navigate it? If he did not go through the narrow, how could he come into the wide?
7.6: “There is also another example: a city is built, and put on a broad field, and is filled with all good.
7.7: “Its entrance is narrow, and is put in a dangerous place to fall, so there is a fire on the right hand, and a deep moat on the left,
7.8: and only one path between them both, even between the fire and the water, so narrow that only one man could go through at once.
7.9: “If this city now were given to a man as an inheritance, if he should never pass the danger placed before it, how shall he receive this inheritance?”
7.10: And I said, “It is so, master.” Then he said to me, “So also is Yisra’ĕl’s portion.
7.11: “Because for their sakes I made the world; and when Aḏam transgressed My Laws, then what is now done was established.
7.12: “Then the entrances of this world were made narrow, full of sorrow and hardship. They are but few and evil, full of dangers, and very laborsome.
7.13: “For the entrances of the greater world were wide and sure, and brought forth incorruptible fruit.
7.14: “If then those who live do not strive to go through these distresses and futilities, they shall never receive that which is laid up for them.
7.15: “Now therefore why do you worry yourself, seeing you are but a corruptible man? And why are you disturbed, for you are only mortal?
7.16: “Why have you not considered in your heart that which is to come, rather than that which is present?”
7.17: Then I answered and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, You have ordained in Your Law, that the righteous should inherit these, but that the wicked should perish.
7.18: “Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer distresses, but have expectancy for the expanse; yet those who have done wickedly have suffered distresses, but shall not see the expanse.”
7.19: And he said to me. “There is no judge above Elohim, and none that has understanding above the Most High.
7.20: “For there are many who perish in this life, because they despise the Law of Elohim that is put before them.
7.21: “For Elohim has given a strict Command to those who came, what they should do to live, even as they came, and what they should observe to avoid punishment.
7.22: “Nevertheless they were not obedient to Him; but spoke against Him, and plotted in vain;
7.23: and deceived themselves by their wicked deeds; and said of the Most High, that He did not exist; and did not know His ways.
7.24: “But they have despised His Torah, and denied His Covenants; they have not been trustworthy in His Laws, and have not performed His works.
7.25: “And therefore, Ezra, emptiness is for the empty, and fullness is for the full.
7.26: “See, the time shall come, that these signs which I have told you shall come to pass, and the bride shall appear, and her coming forth shall be seen, which now is withheld from the earth.
7.27: “And whoever is delivered from the evils spoken of shall see My wonders.
7.28: “For My Bĕn 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 shall be revealed with those who are with Him, and those who remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.
7.29: “After these years Ha’Mashiaḥ My Bĕn shall die, and all men who have life.
7.30: “And the world shall be turned into the silence of old seven days, as in the former judgments; so that no one remains.
7.31: “And after seven days, the world that is not yet awake, shall be raised up, and that which is corrupt shall die,
7.32: and the earth shall restore those who are asleep within, and the dust and the secret places shall deliver those who dwell in silence, and those beings who were given to them.
7.33: “And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and anguish shall pass away, and patience shall come to an end.
7.34: “But only judgment shall remain, truth shall stand, and belief shall grow strong.
7.35: And the works shall follow, and the rewards be revealed, and the good deeds shall be firm, and wicked deeds shall not reign.
7.36: “The pit of torture shall appear, and opposite shall be the place of rest; and the furnace of Gĕy-Hinnom shall be uncovered and the paradise of delight opposite.
7.37: “Then the Most High shall say to the nations that have been raised from the dead, ‘See, and know whom you have denied, whom you have not served, whose Commands you have despised.
7.38: ‘Look on this side and that; here is delight and rest, and there are fire and torture.’ So He shall speak to them on the day of judgment;
7.39: a day that has no sun or moon or stars,
7.40: or cloud or thunder or lightning, or wind or water or air, or darkness or evening or morning,
7.41: or summer or spring or heat, or winter or frost or cold, or hail or rain or dew,
7.42: or noon or night, or dawn or shining or bright light, but only the splendor of the esteem of the Most High, by which all shall see what has been appointed.
7.43: “It shall last as if for a week of years.
7.44: “This is My judgment and its appointed order; and to you alone have I shown these.”
7.45: And I answered and said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, I said then and say now: Ashrĕ are those who are alive and guard Your Commandments!
7.46: “But what of those for whom I prayed? For who among the living have not sinned, or who is there among mortal man that has not transgressed Your Covenant?
7.47: “And now I see that the world to come shall bring delight to few, but torture to many.
7.48: “For an evil heart has grown up within us which has separated us from Elohim, and has brought us into corruption and the ways of death, and has shown us the paths of destruction and removed us far from ḥai; and not only for a few, but for almost all who have been created.”
7.49: And he answered me and said, “Listen to me Ezra, and I will teach you, and shall admonish you once more.
7.50: “For this reason the Most High has not made one world, but two.
7.51: “Because you have said that the righteous are few, while the wicked are many; hear the explanation for this.
7.52: If you have only a few precious stones, would you add lead and clay to them?
7.53: And I said, “Aḏonai, how could this be?”
7.54: And He said to me, “Not only this, but ask the earth and it shall tell you; submit to it and it shall declare to you;
7.55: and say to it, ‘You produce gold and silver and copper, and also iron and lead and clay;
7.56: but silver is more plentiful than gold, and copper than silver, and iron than copper, and lead than iron, and clay than lead.’
7.57: “So judge which is more precious and desirable, that which is plentiful or that which is rare?”
7.58: And I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who reigns, what is plentiful is of less value, for what is rare is more precious.”
7.59: And He answered me and said, “Consider within yourself what you have thought, for the one who has what is hard to obtain rejoices more than the one who has what is plentiful.
7.60: “So also shall be the judgement that I have promised; for I shall rejoice over the few who are saved, because it is they who have made My esteem prevail, and through them My Name has been esteemed.
7.61: “I shall not grieve over the great number of those who perish; for they are like mist, and are similar to a flame and smoke - they are lit on fire and burn with heat, and are extinguished.”
7.62: And I replied and said, “O earth, what have you brought forth, if the mind is made out of dust like the other creations?
7.63: “For it would have been better if the dust itself had not been brought forth, so that the mind might not have been made from it.
7.64: “But now the mind grows with us, and therefore we are tortured, because we perish and we know it.
7.65: “Let mankind lament, but let the beasts of the field be glad; let all who have been born lament, but let the cattle and flocks rejoice.
7.66: “It is much better for them than for us; for they do not look to a judgment, and they do not know of any torture or deliverance promised to them after death.
7.67: “What does it profit us if our life is preserved but we are cruelly tortured?
7.68: “For all who are born are entangled in wickedness, and are full of sins and burdened with transgressions.
7.69: “And if we are not to come into judgement after death, perhaps it would have been better for us.”
7.70: And he answered me and said, “When the Most High made the world and Aḏam and all who have come from him, He first prepared the judgment and that which pertains to the judgment.
7.71: “But now, know from your own words, for you have said that the mind grows with us.
7.72: “For this reason, therefore, those who live on earth shall be tortured, for though they had knowledge, they committed wickedness; and although they received the Commandments, they did not guard them; and though they obtained the Law, they dealt untrustworthily with what they had received.
7.73: “What then shall they have to say in the judgment, or how shall they answer in the last days?
7.74: “How long the Most High has been patient with the inhabitants of the world! And not for their sakes, but because of the days that He has ordained.”
7.75: And I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, show this also to your servant: whether after death, as soon as every one of us breathes their last, we shall be kept in rest until those days come when You shall renew the creation, or whether we shall be tortured immediately?
7.76: And he answered me and said, “I shall show you this also, but do not include yourself with those who have mocked, or number yourself among those who are tortured.
7.77: “For you have a treasure of work stored up with the Most High, but it shall not be shown to you till the last days.
7.78: “And concerning death, the teaching is: when the decisive decree goes forth from the Most High, that one shall die, as the spirit leaves the body to return to Him again who gave it, first of all it adores the esteem of the Most High.
7.79: “If it is one of those who has mocked and has not guarded the Way of the Most High, who has despised His Law and hated those who revere Elohim;
7.80: such spirits do not enter into dwellings, but shall immediately wander in torture, forever in grief and sorrow in seven ways.
7.81: “The first way, because they have mocked the Law of the Most High.
7.82: “The second way, because they cannot make a good repentance so that they now may live.
7.83: “The third way, they shall see the reward laid up for those who have trusted the Covenants of the Most High.
7.84: “The fourth way, they shall consider the torture laid up for themselves in the last days.
7.85: “The fifth way, they shall see how the dwellings of the others are guarded by messengers in deep rest.
7.86: “The sixth way, they shall see how some of them pass over into torture.
7.87: “The seventh way, which is greater than all the ways that have been spoken, because they shall utterly waste away in confusion and be consumed with shame, and shall wither with fear at seeing the esteem of the Most High in whose presence they sinned while they were alive, and in whose presence they are to be judged in the last days.
7.88: “And this is the order for those who have guarded the Ways of the Most High, when they are separated from their mortal body:
7.89: “During the time that they lived in it, they labored to serve the Most High, and withstood danger every hour so they might guard the Law of the Lawgiver perfectly.
7.90: “Therefore this is the teaching concerning them:
7.91: “Firstly, they shall see with great joy the esteem of He who receives him, for they shall have rest in seven orders.
7.92: “The first order, because they strove with great effort to overcome the wicked thought that was formed with them, so that it might not lead them astray from ḥai unto death.
7.93: “The second order, because they see the confusion in which the beings of the unrighteous wander and the punishment that awaits them.
7.94: “The third order, they see the witness that He who formed them bears concerning them, that throughout their life they guarded the Law with which they were entrusted.
7.95: “The fourth order, they know the rest that they now enjoy, being gathered into their rooms and guarded by messengers in deep rest, and the esteem waiting for them in the last days.
7.96: “The fifth order, they rejoice that they have now escaped what is corruptible and shall inherit what is to come; and they also see the difficulty and toil from which they have been delivered, and the spacious freedom that they are to receive and enjoy in immortality.
7.97: “The sixth order, when it is shown them how their face is to shine like the sun, and how they are to be made like the light of the stars, being incorruptible from then on.
7.98: “The seventh order, which is greater than all that have been spoken, for they shall rejoice with boldness, and shall be confident without confusion, and shall be glad without fear, for they press forward to see the face of He whom they served in life and from whom they are to receive their reward when esteemed.
7.99: “This is the order of the beings of the righteous, which from now on is announced; and the previously spoken are the ways of torture that those who would not pay heed shall suffer from now on.”
7.100: Then I answered and said, “Shall there be time given to the beings after they have been separated from the bodies, to see what you have described to me?”
7.101: And he said to me, “They shall have freedom for seven days, so that during these seven days they may see that of which you have been told, and afterwards they shall be gathered into their dwellings.”
7.102: And I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, show further to me, your servant, whether on the day of judgment the righteous shall be able to intercede for the unrighteous or to entreat the Most High for them -
7.103: fathers for sons or sons for parents, brothers for brothers, relatives for their relatives or friends for those who are most dear.”
7.104: And he answered me and said, “Since you have found favor in my eyes, I will show you this also. The day of judgment is certain and displays to all the sign of truth. Just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his servant, or a friend his dearest friend, to be sick or sleep or eat or be healed in his place,
7.105: so no one shall ever pray for another on that day, neither shall anyone lay a burden on another, for then all shall bear their own righteousness and unrighteousness.”
7.106: Then I said, “Aḇraham prayed first for the Seḏomites, and Mosheh for the fathers that sinned in the wilderness;
7.107: and Yahoshua after him for Yisra’ĕl in the time of Aḵan;
7.108: and Shemu’ĕl and Dawiḏ for the destruction; and Shelomoh for those who would come to the Miqdash;
7.109: and Ĕliyahu for those who received rain; and for the dead, that he might live;
7.110: and Ḥizqiyahu for the people in the time of Sanḥĕriḇ; and many for many.
7.111: “Even so now, seeing corruption has grown, and wickedness increased, and the righteous have prayed for the wicked; why shall it also not be so now?”
7.112: He answered me, and said, “This present life is not the end where much esteem dwells; therefore they have prayed for the weak.
7.113: “But the day of judgment shall be the end of this age, and the beginning of the immortality to come, in which corruption is past.
7.114: “Lack of self control is at an end, whoring is cut off, righteousness growns, and truth springs forth.
7.115: “Then no man shall be able to save he who is destroyed, nor to oppress he who has overcome.”
7.116: Then I answered and said, “This is my first and last saying: that it would have been better to not have given the earth to Aḏam; or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.
7.117: “For what profit is there for men here in this present time to live in heaviness, and to look for punishment after death?
7.118: “O you Aḏam, what have you done? For though it was you that sinned, you have not fallen alone, but all of us who come from you.
7.119: “For what does it profit us, if there is promised us an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?
7.120: “Or that there is an everlasting expectancy promised to us, whereas we being most wicked are made worthless?
7.121: “Or that there are dwellings of healing and safety laid up for us, whereas we have lived wickedly?
7.122: “And that the esteem of the Most High is kept to defend those who have led a watchful life, whereas we have walked in the most wicked ways of all?
7.123: “And that there should be shown a paradise, whose fruit endures forever, where there is safety and healing, since we shall not enter into it,
7.124: for we have walked in crooked places?
7.125: “Or that the faces of those who have practiced self-control shall shine above the stars, whereas our faces shall be blacker than darkness?
7.126: “For while we lived and committed wickedness, we did not consider that we should begin to suffer for it after death.”
7.127: Then he answered me, and said, “This is the condition of the battle, that man who is born upon the earth shall fight;
7.128: that, if he is overcome, he shall suffer as you have said; but if he overcomes, he shall receive that which I say.
7.129: “For this is the life of which Mosheh spoke to the people while he lived, saying, ‘Choose life, that you may live.’
7.130: “Nevertheless they did not believe him, nor even the neḇi’im after him, nor myself who has spoken to them,
7.131: that there should not be such grief in their destruction, as shall be the joy over those who are persuaded to deliverance.”
7.132: Then I answered, and said, “I know, master, that the Most High is called kind, in that He has kindness upon those who have not yet come into the world,
7.133: and upon those who also turn to His Law;
7.134: and that He is patient, and endures those who have sinned, as His creatures;
7.135: and that He is generous, for He is ready to give where needed;
7.136: and that He is of great kindness, for He multiplies more and more kindnesses to those who are present, and are past, and also to those who are to come.
7.137: “For if He did not multiply His kindnesses, the world would not continue with those who inherit therein.
7.138: “And He pardons; for if He did not do so of his goodness, and those who have committed wickednesses were forgiven them, the ten thousandth part of mankind would not remain living.
7.139: “And being Judge, if He did not forgive those who are healed by His Word, and blot out the great number of sins,
7.140: there would likely be very few left in an innumerable crowd!”

8.1: And he answered me, saying, “The Most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.
8.2: “I shall tell you a parable, Ezra; just as when you ask the earth, it shall say to you, that it gives much clay from which earthen vessels are made, but little dust from which gold comes; even so is the course of this present world.
8.3: “There are many created, but few shall be saved.”
8.4: So I answered and said, “O my being, swallow down understanding, and devour wisdom.
8.5: “For you have come here against your desire, and against it you depart; for you no longer have but a short time to live.
8.6: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, if You would allow Your servant, that we may pray before You, and You give us a seed to our heart, and tend to our understanding, that fruit may come from it; for how shall each man live who is corrupt, who bears the likeness of man?
8.7: “For You are alone, and we are all one workmanship of Your hands, as You have said.
8.8: “For when the body is formed in the mother’s womb, and You give it members, Your creation is preserved in fire and water, and nine months Your workmanship endures Your creation which is created in her.
8.9: “But that which keeps and is kept shall both be preserved; and when the time comes, the womb delivers up that which grew in it.
8.10: “For You have commanded from the members of the body, that is, out of the breasts, milk to be given, which is the fruit of the breasts,
8.11: so that what has been formed may be nourished for a time, till You lead it to Your kindness.
8.12: “You brought it up with Your righteousness, and instructed it in Your Law, and instructed it with Your Right-Ruling.
8.13: “And You shall put it to death as Your creation, and revive it as Your work.
8.14: “If therefore You destroy that which was formed with such great labor, it is easy to be appointed by Your command, that that which was made might be preserved.
8.15: “Now therefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I shall speak; regarding mankind in general whom You know best; and regarding Your people, for whose sake I am grieved;
8.16: and for Your inheritance, for whose cause I mourn; and for Yisra’ĕl, for whom I am burdened; and for Ya’aqoḇ, for whose sake I am troubled.
8.17: “Therefore I shall begin to pray before You for myself and for them; for I see the fall of we who dwell in the land,
8.18: and I have heard the swiftness of the judgment to come.
8.19: “Therefore hear my voice, and understand my words, and I shall speak before You.” This is the beginning of the words of Ezra, before he was taken up: and I said,
8.20: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You who dwells forever, who sees from above that which is in the shamayim and in the air;
8.21: whose throne is beyond measure; whose esteem cannot be contained; before whom the hosts of messengers stand with trembling;
8.22: whose deeds are accompanied by wind and fire; whose Word is true, and whose words are forever; whose Command is strong, and Law reverent;
8.23: whose look dries up the depths, and whose wrath makes the mountains melt away; which the truth witnesses.
8.24: “O hear the prayer of Your servant, and listen to the petition of Your creation.
8.25: “For while I live I shall speak, and so long as I have understanding I shall answer.
8.26: “O do not look upon the sins of Your people; but on those who serve You in truth.
8.27: “Do not heed the wicked devices of the gentiles, but the desire of those who guard Your Witnesses in afflictions.
8.28: “Do not think upon those who have walked falsely before You; but remember those who have known Your reverence according to Your desire.
8.29: “Let it not be Your desire to destroy those who have lived like beasts; but to look upon those who have clearly taught Your Law.
8.30: “Do not be wroth with those who are deemed worse than beasts; but love those who always put their trust in Your righteousness and esteem.
8.31: “For we and our fathers languish of such sicknesses; but because of we sinners You shall be called kind.
8.32: “For if You have a desire to show favor upon us, You shall be called kind, namely by us, who have no works of righteousness.
8.33: “For the righteous, who have many good works laid up with You, shall receive reward for their own deeds.
8.34: “For what is mankind, that You should take displeasure in him; or what is a corruptible generation, that You should be so bitter toward it?
8.35: “For in truth there is no man among them who is born, except he who has done wickedly; and among the trustworthy there is none who has not done wrong.
8.36: “For in this, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Your righteousness and Your goodness shall be declared, if You are kind to those who do not have the trust of good works.”
8.37: Then He answered me, and said, “Some matters you have spoken rightly, and according to your words it shall be.
8.38: “For indeed I shall not think upon the works of those who have sinned before death, before judgment, before destruction;
8.39: but I shall rejoice over the works of the righteous, and I shall also remember their sojournings, and the deliverance, and the reward, that they shall have.
8.40: “As I have spoken now, so it shall come to pass.
8.41: “For as the farmer sows much seed on the ground, and plants many trees, and yet that which is well sown in its season does not come up, neither does all that is planted take root; even so it is as those who are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.”
8.42: I answered then and said, “If I have found favor, let me speak.
8.43: “As the farmer’s seed perishes, if it does not come up, and does not receive Your rain in due season; or if there is too much rain, and ruins it;
8.44: even so, mankind also perishes, who is formed with Your hands, and is called Your own likeness, because he is made like You, for whose sake You have made all, and likened him to the farmer’s seed.
8.45: “Do not be wroth with us but spare Your people, and show favor upon Your own inheritance; for You are kind to Your creation.”
8.46: Then He answered me, and said, “That which is present is for the present, and that which is to come for what is to come.
8.47: “For you come far short that you should be able to love My creation more than I; but I have often drawn near to you, and unto it, but never to the unrighteous.
8.48: “In this also you are praiseworthy before the Most High;
8.49: in that you have humbled yourself, as is proper, and have not judged yourself worthy to be much esteemed among the righteous.
8.50: “For many great hardships shall come upon those who dwell in the world in the latter days, because they have walked in great pride.
8.51: “But understand for yourself, and seek out the esteem of those who are like you.
8.52: “For to you paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, abundance is made ready, a city is built, and rest is given, even perfect goodness and wisdom.
8.53: “The root of evil is sealed up from you, sickness and the moth is hidden from you, and corruption has fled into She’ol to be forgotten;
8.54: sorrows have passed, and in the end the treasure of immortality is shown.
8.55: “And therefore ask no more questions concerning the multitude of those who perish;
8.56: for when they had received freedom, they despised the Most High, scorned His Law, and forsook His Ways.
8.57: “And they have trodden down His righteous ones,
8.58: and said in their heart, ‘There is no Elohim,’ and even knowing that they shall die.
8.59: “For as that which is spoken of shall receive you, so thirst and anguish are prepared for them; for it was not His desire that men should come to naught;
8.60: but those who are created have defiled the Name of He who made them, and were thankless to He who prepared life for them.
8.61: “And therefore My judgment is now at hand.
8.62: “I have not shown these matters to all men, but to you, and a few like you.” Then I answered and said,
8.63: “See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, now You have shown me the multitude of the wonders, which You shall begin to do in the last times; but You have not shown me at what time.”

9.1: Then He answered me, and said, “Measure the time diligently in itself; and when you see some of the signs past, which I have told you before,
9.2: then you shall understand, that it is the very same time, wherein the Most High shall begin to avenge the world which He made.
9.3: “Therefore when there are seen earthquakes and the people of the world in uproar;
9.4: then you shall understand well, that the Most High spoke of those matters from the days that were before you, even from the beginning.
9.5: “For as all that is made in the world has a beginning and an end, and the end is manifest;
9.6: so also the times of the Most High have clear beginnings in wonder and works of power, and endings in signs and wonders.
9.7: “And everyone that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by belief, by which you have believed,
9.8: shall survive the dangers spoken of, and shall see My deliverance in My land, and within My borders; for I have qadosh them for Myself from the beginning.
9.9: “Then those who have abused My Ways shall be in a wretched state; and those who have thrown them away in spite shall dwell in torture.
9.10: “For such have received benefits in their life, but have not known Me;
9.11: and those who have loathed My Law, while they still had freedom, and when a place for repentance was still open to them, did not understand, but despised it;
9.12: the same must acknowledge it in anguish after death.
9.13: “And therefore do not question how the wicked shall be punished, and when; but inquire how the righteous shall be delivered, to whom the world belongs, and for whom the world is created.”
9.15: “I have said before, and now speak, and shall also speak it after, that there are many more of those who perish, than of those who shall be delivered;
9.16: as a wave is greater than a drop!”
9.17: And He answered me, saying, “As the field is, so is the seed also; as are the flowers, such are the colors also; as the workman is, such is the work also; and as the farmer is himself, so is his harvest also; for it was the time for the world.
9.18: “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for those to dwell within who now live, no man spoke against Me.
9.19: “For then everyone obeyed; but now the way of those who are created in this world that is made are a corrupted seed forever, and rid themselves of the Law which is unsearchable.
9.20: “So I considered the world, and see, there was danger because of the schemes that were brought into it.
9.21: “And I saw, and spared it greatly, and have kept for Myself a grape of the cluster, and a plant of a great people.
9.22: “Let the multitude perish then, who were brought forth in ruin; and let My grape be kept, and My plant; for with great labor I have made it perfect.
9.23: “Nevertheless, if you shall wait yet seven more days, and you do not fast in them,
9.24: but go into a field of flowers, where no house is built, and eat only the flowers of the field; taste no meat, drink no wine, but eat flowers only.
9.25: “And pray to the Most High continually, then I shall come and speak with you.”
9.26: So I went my way into the field which is called Arpaḏ, as He commanded me; and I sat there among the flowers, and ate of the plants of the field, and the food they gave satisfied me.
9.27: After seven days I sat on the grass, and my heart was tortured within me, as before;
9.28: and I opened my mouth, and began to speak before the Most High, and said,
9.29: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You who show Yourself to us, You were shown to our fathers in the wilderness, in a place where no man treads, in a barren place, when they came out of Mitsrayim.
9.30: “And You spoke saying, ‘Hear Me, O Yisra’ĕl; and guard My Words, you seed of Ya’aqoḇ.
9.31: ‘For look, I sow My Torah in you, and it shall bear fruit in you, and you shall be esteemed in it forever.’
9.32: “But our fathers, who received the Torah, did not guard it, and did not observe Your Laws; and though the fruit of Your Torah did not perish, nor could it, for it was Yours;
9.33: yet those who received it perished, because they did not guard that which was sown in them.
9.34: “And see, it is the manner, when the ground has received seed, or the sea a ship, or any vessel food or drink, that, that in which it was sown or thrown into is perished,
9.35: that which was sown, or thrown in, or received, also perishes, and does not remain with us; but with us it has not come to be.
9.36: “For we who have received the Law perish by sin, and our heart also which received it,
9.37: however the Law does not perish, but remains enforced.”
9.38: And when I spoke these matters in my heart, I looked back with my eyes, and on the right side I saw a woman, and see, she mourned and wept with a loud voice, and was very grieved in heart, and her garments were torn, and she had ashes upon her head.
9.39: Then I dismissed my thoughts that I was in, and I turned to her,
9.40: and said to her, “Why do you weep? Why are you so grieved in your heart?”
9.41: And she said to me, “Master, leave me alone, that I may bewail myself, and add to my sorrow, for I am very troubled in my heart, and brought very low.”
9.42: And I said to her, “Tell me, what troubles you?”
9.43: She said to me, “I your servant have been barren, and had no child, though I had a husband thirty years,
9.44: and those thirty years I did naught day and night, and every hour, but make my prayer to the Most High.
9.45: “After thirty years Elohim heard me, your female servant, looked upon my misery, considered my trouble, and gave me a son; and I was very pleased with him, as was my husband also, and all my neighbors; and we gave great esteem to the Almighty,
9.46: and I provided for him with great struggles.
9.47: “So when he grew up, and came to the time that he should have a wife, I made a feast.
